data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 proposes testing the stability of the correlation structure under environmental perturbation as the distinguishing evidence. But the causal mechanism is underspecified and partly circular: to identify a correlation structure as 'stable under perturbation,' one must already know which perturbations are legitimate environmental changes versus which are the shared causes themselves. If the 'shared stable environment' whose change reveals hidden dependence is the very kind of common dependency that causes correlated failure (e.g., shared cloud provider), then the test reduces to 'if the shared cause fails, failures correlate'—which is the phenomenon to be detected, not a discriminating mechanism. SRC_002 never supplies a causal criterion that separates a perturbation that merely stresses the same shared cause from one that genuinely tests independence, so the evidence criterion cannot do the distinguishing work the problem demands.
